import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 2, "n_minibatches": 16, "ent_coef": 0.005}


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        place = self.head(f)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
LH = 64
LF = 32
LP = 16
LM = 32

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 2, "n_minibatches": 16, "ent_coef": 0.005}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = int(spec.Z)
        Z = self.Z
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in spec.footprints]
        lin = 4 * (2 * Z - 1) + 3 + Z
        self.lstem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(lin, LH, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(LH, LF, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.lproj = nn.Conv2d(LF, LP, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * LP, LM, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(LM, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH + LF, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def layer_input(self, obs):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        st = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        st = F.pad(st, (0, 0, 0, 0, Z - 1, Z - 1))
        rel = torch.stack([st[:, :, z:z + 2 * Z - 1] for z in range(Z)], dim=1)
        rel = rel.reshape(B, Z, 4 * (2 * Z - 1), Y, X)
        rest = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(1).expand(B, Z, 3, Y, X)
        eye = torch.eye(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype)
        oh = eye[None, :, :, None, None].expand(B, Z, Z, Y, X)
        inp = torch.cat([rel, rest, oh], dim=2)
        return inp.reshape(B * Z, inp.shape[2], Y, X)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        h = self.lstem(self.layer_input(obs))
        p = self.lproj(h)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            res.append(out(F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))))
        sc = torch.cat(res, dim=1)
        T = sc.shape[1]
        place = sc.reshape(B, Z, T, Y, X).sum(1).flatten(1)
        f = F.relu(self.c1(self.stem(obs)))
        hl = h.reshape(B, Z, LF, Y, X).mean((1, 3, 4))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3)), hl], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

STEM = 64
COL = 48
WIDTH = 40
PROJ = 32
HID = 32
HEADS = 4

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 2, "n_minibatches": 16, "ent_coef": 0.005}


class Attn(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, heads, n):
        super().__init__()
        self.h = heads
        self.d = c // heads
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(c)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(c, 3 * self.h * self.d)
        self.out = nn.Linear(self.h * self.d, c)
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, n, c))

    def forward(self, f):
        B, C, Y, X = f.shape
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        u = self.norm(t + self.pos)
        q, k, v = self.qkv(u).chunk(3, dim=-1)
        q = q.reshape(B, -1, self.h, self.d).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.reshape(B, -1, self.h, self.d).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.reshape(B, -1, self.h, self.d).transpose(1, 2)
        a = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(self.d), dim=-1)
        o = torch.matmul(a, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, -1, self.h * self.d)
        t = t + self.out(o)
        return t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, C, Y, X)


class PoolHead(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, c, footprints, proj, hid):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(a), int(b)) for a, b in footprints]
        self.proj = nn.Conv2d(c, proj, 1)
        self.mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * proj, hid, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.outs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(hid, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])

    def forward(self, f):
        p = self.proj(f)
        res = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.mix, self.outs):
            if dy * dx == 1:
                mx, mn, av = p, p, p
            else:
                q = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
                mx = F.max_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                mn = -F.max_pool2d(-q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
                av = F.avg_pool2d(q, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            res.append(out(h))
        return torch.cat(res, dim=1).flatten(1)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        n = int(spec.Y) * int(spec.X)
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, STEM, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(STEM, COL, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(COL, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.attn = Attn(WIDTH, HEADS, n)
        self.head = PoolHead(WIDTH, spec.footprints, PROJ, HID)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        s = self.stem(obs)
        x = F.relu(self.c1(s))
        f = F.relu(x + self.c2(x))
        f2 = F.relu(self.attn(f))
        place = self.head(f2)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f2.mean((2, 3)), f2.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

There are no results yet, and scores stay hidden for the whole search. The only feedback I will get is whether a trial crashed, timed out or failed a check. So each proposal has to be a sensible bet on its own, and all three must run without errors.

The starting network costs about 3.2M multiply-adds per sample. Anything bigger reduces the number of training samples one for one, while anything smaller earns no extra samples. The default recipe gives about 131k steps, or only 32 updates.

My two bets are:
- Cut the PPO epochs to buy more fresh data. Episodes are short and the designs vary a lot, so seeing more designs probably beats reusing the same ones.
- Give every cell cheap global context. Placement order depends on the whole design, for example where overhangs are and what is still missing elsewhere, but two 3x3 convolutions only see a 5x5 patch.

All three candidates keep the compute cost (FLOPs) near the starting network's, and none uses 3D convolutions, to avoid the time limit.
analyses.2: No scores are visible. All three round-1 trials trained without errors, and none came close to the time or compute limits. So the evidence only tells us what runs, not what works better. Reasoning about the task instead: whether a placement is correct depends on its landing layer, which is the highest build column under the footprint. The brick's cells at that layer must be missing from the build, and the target must be empty in any gap the brick would seal. The baseline pools 2D features that mix all layers together, so it has to work out this layer arithmetic indirectly. The main new idea is a per-layer placement head: each layer z gets shared features from build and target columns re-indexed relative to z, pooled over each footprint, and the per-layer scores are summed. Two of this round's candidates use it, one alone and one with spatial context from the trunk. The third candidate refines r1c2 with a longer credit horizon, which should help the exact-build bonus. All candidates use 2 PPO epochs so the sample count stays near or above the baseline.

Five of them use 2 PPO epochs, with about 200k–230k steps for the cheaper ones, so the 900 s limit is not binding there. So far the search has tested 2D global context (r1c2), a longer horizon (r2c2), a dilated deeper trunk (r1c3) and per-layer placement heads (r2c1, r2c3). Three directions remain untested and can still inform the final round:
(1) More fresh data: 1 PPO epoch roughly doubles the number of designs seen.
(2) Full spatial self-attention, so each cell can compare its column with any other column. This matters for ordering decisions, such as filling under a planned overhang before sealing it.
(3) The structured per-layer head with more data.
Each candidate makes one main change from an existing trial, so the hidden scores can still be attributed when the final selection is made.
analyses.4: No scores are visible, so the evidence is only that every design trained without error and stayed within the time limit. The final pick will go to the highest 2-seed dev score. Since this is the last round, the most useful candidates are strong combinations of ideas that each had a sound reason behind them. Those ideas are: more fresh samples (fewer PPO epochs), a longer credit horizon for the bonus that arrives only at episode end, global context, and the per-layer footprint head that matches how bricks land. The global-context trunk is the cheapest network (about 1.04x compute), so it can see the most data. The per-layer head is the best match to the task's structure but has never been tested with a longer horizon or with any spatial mixing inside each layer. I propose: (1) the 1-epoch global-context net plus gamma 0.98; (2) the per-layer head plus gamma 0.98; (3) the per-layer head plus a 3x3 convolution inside each layer, so it can see neighbouring support and overhang structure at that layer.
